title: Why Is Venice Sinking? — 60-second studio sample

scenes.narration: Venice is sinking. This extraordinary city built on water is slowly losing its fight against the sea.
scenes.rationale: Visual Director: narration beat is cold open; rendered with remotion using globe zoom title and a push in camera.

scenes.narration: It sits inside a shallow lagoon on Italy's Adriatic coast, spread across more than a hundred islands, with three narrow inlets connecting it to the open sea.
scenes.rationale: Visual Director: narration beat is map context; rendered with remotion using map highlight arrows and a pan right camera.

scenes.narration: Waterlogged, oxygen-poor mud preserves the piles, but anaerobic bacteria still attack wood. Slow decay and the wood-water-soil system maintain stability.
scenes.rationale: Visual Director: narration beat is engineering demo; rendered with remotion using cross section build and a pan down camera.

scenes.narration: But the sediment keeps compacting. Industrial groundwater pumping accelerated the sinking until the nineteen seventies. In nineteen sixty-six, a record surge reached one hundred and ninety-four centimetres.
scenes.rationale: Visual Director: narration beat is data chart; rendered with remotion using animated bars datum guide and a static camera.

scenes.narration: So Italy built MOSE: seventy-eight hollow steel gates that rest on the seabed, then swing upward on compressed air to hold the Adriatic back.
scenes.rationale: Visual Director: narration beat is engineering demo; rendered with remotion using mechanism animation and a static camera.

scenes.narration: The shield has held back major tides. But Venice still sinks, the sea still rises, and this city is not alone.
scenes.rationale: Visual Director: narration beat is comparison montage; rendered with remotion using world zoom markers and a pull back camera.
